ev.q: The percentage of teens aged 15–19 years who used LARC varied widely by state, from 0.7% (Mississippi) to 25.8% (Colorado).
Use of LARC was higher among teens aged 18–19 years (7.6%) versus 15–17 years (6.5%) (p<0.001).
the percentage who adopted or continued use of LARC at their last visit increased from 0.4% (2005) to 7.1% (2013)
the number of LARC users increased from 4,112 (2005) to 43,696 (2013).
Of the 616,148 female teens seeking contraceptive services in 2013, 17,349 (2.8%) used IUDs, and 26,347 (4.3%) used implants.
Use of LARC was higher among teens aged 18–19 years (7.6%) versus 15–17 years (6.5%) (p<0.001).
For both age groups, the increase in use of implants exceeded the increase in use of IUDs
Trends over time and by age, region, and type of service site were evaluated using the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test statistic.
The Family Planning Annual Report contains data from all entities that receive Title X grants
Use of LARC among teens* seeking contraceptive services at Title X service sites increased from 0.4% in 2005 to 7.1% in 2013
